definitions.explanation: A nocturnal bird of prey with large forward-facing eyes, a flat face, and silent flight. Owls are associated with wisdom and good luck in Japan.

examples.japanese: {梟|ふくろう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{夜行性|やこうせい}→夜行性：16217_yakousei⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
⟦お{土産|みやげ}→お土産：01353_omiyage⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{梟|ふくろう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{置物|おきもの}→置物：19885_okimono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: I bought an owl figurine as a souvenir.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夜|よる}→夜：00487_yoru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{森|もり}→森：02260_mori⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歩|ある}いていたら→歩く：00538_aruku⟧、{梟|ふくろう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鳴|な}き{声|ごえ}→鳴き声：16846_nakigoe⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{聞|き}こえてきた→聞こえる：01229_kikoeru⟧。
examples.english: While walking through the forest at night, I heard the hooting of an owl.

notes:
{梟|ふくろう} refers to owls.

Alternative writing: フクロウ (katakana, common)

Common expressions:
- {梟|ふくろう}⟦カフェ→カフェ：06767_kafe⟧ (owl café)
- {梟|ふくろう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{置物|おきもの}→置物：19885_okimono⟧ (owl figurine)

Counter: ⟦{羽|わ}→羽：01007_wa⟧

Cultural note:
In Japan, {梟|ふくろう} is considered a lucky symbol. The word can be written with different kanji to create puns:
- ⟦{不苦労|ふくろう}→不苦労：noentry⟧ ("no hardship")
- ⟦{福来郎|ふくろう}→福来郎：noentry⟧ ("good fortune comes")

Owl figurines and goods are popular as good luck charms. Owl cafés where visitors can interact with owls have become tourist attractions in Japan.
